To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the V1 neuron's orientation selectivity can be generated by both tuned enhancement (near the preferred orientation) and global suppression (from all orientations), and that the tuned suppression can be broader than the tuned enhancement.
1) The dynamics of orientation tuning in the V1 neurons of macaque monkeys is dominated by both tuned enhancement (near the cell's preferred stimulus orientation) and global suppression.

(1) V1 orientation selectivity is created by a combination of both tuned enhancement and cortical inhibition; (2) the enhancement is supplied by the thalamocortical input, plus amplification by cortical interaction; (3) the inhibition is supplied by cortical interneurons; and (4) these mechanisms also can explain steady-state orientation selectivity in the neuron population.

the orientation selectivity of V1 neurons is a result of the combined action of both cortical excitation and cortical inhibition, which are both orientation selective.

the V1 neuron's orientation selectivity results mainly from both tuned enhancement and suppression, with the suppression supplied by cortical inhibition and the enhancement supplied by feedforward input (plus amplification from cortical-cortical interactions).

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cortical inhibition is important for the generation of orientation selectivity.
the cortical inhibition is important for the orientation selectivity in the primary visual cortex.
the dynamics and steady-state orientation selectivity are determined mainly by the interaction of tuned enhancement and global (or local) suppression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cortical inhibition is a very important mechanism in the brain.
the dynamics of cortical neurons is very important for understanding the mechanisms of orientation selectivity and other aspects of visual processing.
the cortical circuits that generate orientation selectivity in V1 are more complex than the simple model of a cell's orientation tuning that is often used in computational modeling of V1.
